intro.text: Awaysis Capital, Inc. is a real estate management and hospitality company focused on the acquisition, redevelopment, ownership, sale, and management of residential vacation properties and resort communities in desirable travel destinations. Our business strategy is to identify and reposition real estate properties that management believes have the potential to generate value through improvements, hospitality operations, residential sales, and property management services. Our operations include the development and management of vacation accommodations, short-term and long-term rentals, and related hospitality and property management activities.

cor.text: New real estate inventory is carried at the lower of cost or net realizable value. The cost of finished inventories determined by the specific identification method is removed from inventories and recorded as a component of cost of sales at the time revenue is recognized. In addition, an allocation of depreciation and amortization is included in cost of goods sold. Under the specific identification method, if finished real estate inventory can be sold for a profit there is no basis to write down the inventory below the lower of cost or net realizable value.

sm.heading: Sales and Marketing Expenses
sm.text: Our sales and marketing expenses consist primarily of salaries, commissions and other personnel-related expenses, which may include share-based compensation, for employees engaged in sales, marketing and support of our products and services, promotional and public relations expenses and management and administration expenses in support of sales and marketing.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: Our general and administrative costs include payroll, employee benefits, and other personnel-related costs, which include share-based compensation, associated with administrative and support staff, as well as legal and accounting costs, insurance costs, depreciation and other administrative fees.

nonop.heading: Other (Income) Expenses
nonop.text: During the fiscal years ended June 30, 2025, and 2024, we incurred other (income) and expense of $25,418 and $32,953, respectively, consisting of mortgage interest income and foreign exchange gains, offset by foreign exchange losses and interest expense.

net.heading: Net Loss
net.text: During the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, and 2024, we recognized net losses of $(2,724,941) and $(7,056,911), respectively. These losses were primarily attributable to accounting, marketing, legal, filing fees and transfer agent fees to sustain the corporate existence of the Company and public company-related expenses, and the continued transition from being a shell company to an operating company. The decrease in net loss from fiscal year 2024 to fiscal year 2025 was a result of increased revenue income with the addition of Chial Mountain Limited and a decrease in salary expense due to a salary bonus of $4,400,000 accrued for in fiscal year 2024.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text: We generated negative cash flows from operating activities in the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, compared to the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024. Net cash flows used in operating activities were $(4,808,550) and $503,108 for the fiscal years ended June 30, 2025, and 2024, respectively.

sbc.text: Our sales and marketing expenses consist primarily of salaries, commissions and other personnel-related expenses, which may include share-based compensation, for employees engaged in sales, marketing and support of our products and services, promotional and public relations expenses and management and administration expenses in support of sales and marketing.

wc.text: As of June 30, 2025, we had cash of $220,909 and had a positive working capital of $152,933, which was mainly from the increase in receivables due to mortgage receivable and inventory construction costs, and the addition of convertible notes and line of credit with BOS Investments, Inc. We have sufficient cash or commitments for funding to satisfy our basic operations for at least 12 months and expect the anticipated cost of development of our first properties to come from pre-sales, investors subscriptions, advances or loans from our principal shareholders and not cash-on-hand. We will need to raise additional cash to satisfy our long-term requirements.

cor.text: During the fiscal years ended June 30, 2026, and 2025, we incurred cost of goods sold of $735,302 and $0, respectively, consisting of the sale of two villas.

sm.heading: Sales and Marketing Expenses
sm.text: Our sales and marketing expenses consist primarily of salaries, commissions, and other personnel-related costs, including share-based compensation, for employees involved in the marketing, promotion, and support of our products and services. These expenses also include advertising, promotional activities, digital marketing initiatives, public relations, brand development, and related administrative and management costs incurred to support our sales and marketing functions.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text:
Our general and administrative expenses consist of payroll, employee benefits, and other personnel-related costs, including share-based compensation, associated with our administrative, finance, legal, and corporate support functions. These expenses also include legal and accounting fees, insurance costs, depreciation, technology and software expenses, occupancy and office-related costs, and other administrative fees necessary to support our overall operations and corporate infrastructure.

Certain officers elected to defer receipt of cash compensation. Such amounts were accrued as liabilities and, upon approval by the Board of Directors, were subsequently settled through the issuance of shares of the Company’s common stock. These non-cash settlements reduced accrued compensation liabilities and increased stockholders’ equity.

nonop.heading: Other (Income) Expenses
nonop.text: During the fiscal years ended June 30, 2026, and 2025, we incurred net other expenses of $42,692 and $25,418, respectively, consisting of mortgage interest income and foreign exchange gains, offset by foreign exchange losses and interest expense.

net.heading: Net Loss
net.text:
During the fiscal years ended June 30, 2026, and 2025, we recognized net losses of $(2,586,639) and $(2,724,941), respectively. These losses were primarily attributable to accounting, marketing, legal, filing fees and transfer agent fees to sustain the corporate existence, comply with a public company reporting obligations and support our increase in operations.

The decrease in net loss from fiscal year 2025 to fiscal year 2026 was principally driven by increased revenue generated from the sale of two villas at Chial, increased revenue and management income, as well as operational factors described above. These improvements were partially offset by the ongoing costs associated with scaling our hospitality operations under the Awaysis brand and preparing for future capital-raising activities.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text: We generated negative cash flows from operating activities in the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, compared to the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025. Net cash flows used in operating activities were $(787,952) and $(4,808,550) for the fiscal years ended June 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. Net cash used in operating activities primarily consisted of selling, marketing, and general operating expenses, as well as increased spending on construction in progress-related costs incurred to prepare properties for sale or rental. The reduction in operating cash outflows year over year reflects improved revenue generation and lower marketing expenditures, partially offset by ongoing operational investments as we continue to scale our hospitality and real estate activities.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
